body.statement:
Let \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) satisfy \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and suppose a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied for every source-consistent recorded stratum. There is a universal \(a>0\) such that a randomized localized geometric-resolution algorithm returns exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\) with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). Its arithmetic construction time and certificate length are at most
\[
(n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\). In particular, for any fixed \(b>0\), if \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then the bound is \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\) depending only on \(a\) and \(b\). The output polynomial is the monic minimal polynomial over \(K_G\), not a whole-fiber eliminant, and \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) contains the covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-infinity, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits whose nonzero product is \(h_{G,e}\). The theorem is conditional on the supplied charts; it does not construct or select them.
body.proof_tex:
Fix one source-consistent recorded stratum and use the notation of \(\mathrm{def:source\mbox{-}prime\mbox{-}chart}\).  Thus \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), \(r\leq 2k\), \(P=\ker\xi\subset K_G[x]\), and validity of the supplied chart gives
\[
 P K_G[x]_{H\Delta}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta},
 \qquad \xi(H\Delta)\neq0,                                   \tag{1}
\]
where \(c=\operatorname{ht}P\), the sequence \(h_1,\ldots,h_c\) is reduced and regular after localization, and \(\Delta\) is a nonzero \(c\)-by-\(c\) Jacobian minor.  Hence (1) defines the localization of the source prime itself, rather than an extensional union of residual components.  The Jacobian minor and regular-sequence hypotheses give a smooth, pure-dimensional principal open subset of dimension
\[
 q=r-c\leq 2k.                                                \tag{2}
\]
The inequation \(H\Delta\neq0\) can be encoded without changing that subset by adjoining a variable \(u\) and the equation \(uH\Delta-1=0\).

Put \(E=K_G(\lambda_e)\).  Since \(d_e(G)<\infty\), \(E/K_G\) is finite; since the characteristic is zero, it is separable.  Its \(d_e(G)\) embeddings into \(\overline{K_G}\) give the distinct conjugates of \(\lambda_e\).  For each embedding \(\tau:E\to\overline{K_G}\), the tensor product \(L\otimes_{E,\tau}\overline{K_G}\) is nonzero: choosing an \(E\)-transcendence basis of \(L\) reduces this assertion to tensoring a finite field extension with an algebraic closure.  The corresponding affine model therefore has a nonempty conjugate component.  Moreover, \(H\Delta\), which is nonzero at the source generic point, remains nonzero on that component.  Generic affine hyperplanes meet each positive-dimensional component properly.  Because there are only finitely many conjugate components, the intersection of the corresponding nonempty open sets of hyperplane choices is nonempty.  Consequently one may choose \(q\) affine linear forms whose successive intersections are transverse, zero-dimensional, and nonempty on every conjugate component.  Equivalently, this is the generic transverse slicing operation covered by \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).  Random choices outside the finitely many associated determinant and leading-form hypersurfaces have this property.

Apply that cited geometric-resolution lemma to the localized regular sequence together with the \(q\) slices.  On a successful choice it returns a finite reduced \(K_G\)-algebra \(B_{\mathfrak C}\), multiplication matrices for the exposed coordinates, and a primitive-element representation.  The lifting circuits in the valid chart recover every eliminated directed coordinate, including \(\lambda_e\), and their substitution into every original residual is zero in the localized source-prime algebra.  Let \(M_{e,\mathfrak C}\) denote multiplication by the recovered \(\lambda_e\) on \(B_{\mathfrak C}\), and set
\[
 \chi_{e,\mathfrak C}(t)=\det(tI-M_{e,\mathfrak C}).           \tag{3}
\]
Every geometric point represented by (3) lies on a base change of the source prime, so its queried coordinate is a conjugate of \(\lambda_e\).  Conversely, the common slicing choice meets every conjugate component, so every conjugate occurs as an eigenvalue in at least one chart.  Taking the squarefree part of the product of the polynomials (3) over all source-consistent recorded strata therefore gives a monic polynomial with exactly the distinct conjugates of \(\lambda_e\) as its roots.  Uniqueness of the monic polynomial with those roots yields
\[
 p_e(t)=\operatorname{sqfree}\!\left(
       \prod_{\mathfrak C}\chi_{e,\mathfrak C}(t)\right),
 \qquad \deg p_e=d_e(G).                                    \tag{4}
\]
Thus (4) reports the single-coordinate degree, independently of the cardinality or dimension of the unsliced full parameter fiber.  The orientation upper-bound theorem additionally gives
\[
 \deg p_e=d_e(G)
 \leq 2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}},                  \tag{5}
\]
but no use of whole-fiber degree is made.

All chart coefficients, multiplication matrices, and lifting maps are elements of \(K_G\) represented by rational arithmetic circuits in the covariance entries.  Determinants, polynomial differentiation, subresultant greatest-common-divisor computation, squarefree extraction, and monic normalization are arithmetic-circuit operations over \(K_G\); hence (4) gives coefficientwise rational circuits for \(p_e\).  Equality (1) prevents a factor belonging only to a different residual component from entering (4).  For every rational lifting identity, clearing denominators produces both a pole factor and an incidence-lifting identity.  Homogenization before slicing produces the projective leading-form factors; the univariate output produces its specialized leading-coefficient and squarefreeness-resultant factors.  The covariance denominators are recorded separately.  Finally, applying \(\mathrm{lem:effective\mbox{-}real\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\) to the original supported residual equations and \(\mathrm{lem:real\mbox{-}algebraic\mbox{-}sampling}\) after exact specialization supplies the real-lifting sign and sample-point circuits.  These finitely many circuits form \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\); after clearing covariance denominators and deleting repetitions, their nonzero product is \(h_{G,e}\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\), this bookkeeping inverts no directed-coordinate expression and so does not discard a pole or an identically zero-over-zero stratum.

It remains to establish the resource and error bounds.  The arbitrary-equation and inequation operations on recorded strata are covered by \(\mathrm{lem:lifting\mbox{-}fiber\mbox{-}equidimensional\mbox{-}decomposition}\), while the regular slices are covered by \(\mathrm{lem:groebner\mbox{-}free\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).  Their complexity bounds, multiplication-matrix linear algebra, and (2) imply that for a universal \(a>0\) the total number of arithmetic operations and output gates is at most
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{a}
 \operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),                        \tag{6}
\]
where \(s=s(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\) and \(\mathfrak d=\mathfrak d(\mathfrak C_{G,e})\).  Every randomized genericity decision is the nonvanishing test of an explicitly constructed chart, transversality, leading-form, lifting, or resultant polynomial.  If their degree bounds are \(d_1,\ldots,d_N\), choose the independently sampled finite-field sets so that each allocated error is at most \(\delta/N\).  The Schwartz--Zippel bound and the union bound then give
\[
 \Pr(\text{some symbolic genericity decision is wrong})
 \leq\sum_{j=1}^N \frac{d_j}{|S_j|}\leq\delta.              \tag{7}
\]
On the complementary event, (1)--(4) show that the returned tuple is exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\).

If \(s\leq n^b\) and \(\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), then, after enlarging a constant to cover \(n\geq2\),
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{a}
 \leq n^{a(\max\{1,b\}+1+b)(k+1)}
 \leq n^{C(k+1)}.                                            \tag{8}
\]
This proves the stated fixed-parameter specialization of (6).

The antecedent is essential to what has been proved: the two cited geometric algorithms solve or decompose equations once the localized reduced chart has been supplied, but neither identifies the embedded source-prime component nor constructs a source-nonzero Jacobian minor with bounded rational circuits over \(K_G\).  The argument therefore constructs and certifies the claimed output exactly under, and only under, the supplied-valid-chart hypothesis.
body.justification: A valid localized reduced source-prime chart is sufficient for exact coordinate minimal-polynomial and specialization-certificate construction.
body.gap: Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy and Lecerf do not select or descend the embedded SEM source prime, and their complexity retains geometric-degree dependence.
body.consumer: This is the exact higher-degree polynomial-output contract for a chart-certified extension of fasttreeid.
